templates.text: The world is a map of internal tensions and releases, a landscape felt through muscle tone and joint angle.

Awareness flows from the core outward, sensing the world through the body's own posture and motion.

Knowing comes from the subtle feedback of tendons and joints, a proprioceptive cartography of self.
The world is understood through the body's boundaries, where contact defines form and pressure defines substance.
Perception is anchored in the deep sense of being a physical entity occupying a precise volume of space.
Experience is filtered through the constant, quiet hum of muscular effort and skeletal alignment.

Awareness is a proprioceptive stream, where every external event is first registered as an internal shift.

Perception is the continuous, unconscious monitoring of joint angles and muscle spindle feedback.
Reality is a dynamic equilibrium, felt as a constant, subtle adjustment of posture to maintain balance.
The infant experiences the environment as an extension of bodily sensation, where space is felt, not seen.

The world is perceived as gradients of resistance and support, mapped proprioceptively before all else.
